newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso slides sharply on speculation, jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso slides sharply on speculation, jitters.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed sharply weaker on Thursday after succumbing to speculative pressure amid market jitters ahead of U.S. employment and unemployment figures due on Friday, traders said.

"Everybody sees very strong U.S. employment data and hence interest rate hikes ahead," a trader said, referring to the July 2 Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rate policy.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 4.15 and 3.9 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9650/7.9680 and 7.9560/7.9600 per dollar.
"Dealers are beginning to look ahead to what U.S. interest rates may do," the trader added.
U.S. unemployment and non-farms payrolls data for May will be released on Friday before trade opens in Mexico's foreign exchange markets.
Traders said the peso was also under pressure from the forthcoming close of the first half of the year on June 30, and from mid-term congressional elections on July 6.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.15 centavos weaker at 7.9285/7.9325 per dollar.
"I think the peso could open weaker tomorrow, and then brokers could take profits (on dollars)," another trader said.
Dealers situated support for the peso at 8.0000 per dollar.
